This code is for use in R to provide the analysis that contributed to the manuscript "Using the National Neonatal Audit Programme (NNAP) to assess the relationship between quality of perinatal care with neonatal mortality and morbidity across the UK"
Authors: K Harris, NR Lawrence, O Adeleye, SJ Clark 

MBRRACE data is downloaded from csv through the online data viewer tool:
https://timms.le.ac.uk/mbrrace-uk-perinatal-mortality/data-viewer/

Download the csv files for total mortality and place them in a folder named "MBRRACE_raw_data/total_mortality" in your working directory

NNAP data is downloaded 
https://www.rcpch.ac.uk/work-we-do/clinical-audits/nnap/data-access

Place NNAP csv files in a folder named "NNAP_raw_data" in your working directory

Ensure the following files are downloaded from the main github page and placed into the correct directory within your working directory:
"manual_unit_level_definition/NNAP_manual_unit_levels_to_add.csv"
"Linking_hospitals_to/hospital_trust_manual_linkage_sheet_master.csv"
"abbreviations_to_load/Abbreviations_to_load.csv"

```{r, load all the NNAP data frames}
#rm(list=ls()) #clear the environment if necessary
library(readxl)
library(stringr) # For easy string manipulation (cleaning file names)
library(dplyr)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Configuration
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Define the folder containing the Excel files
# IMPORTANT: Replace "path/to/your/NNAP_raw_data" with the actual path
folder_path <- "NNAP_raw_data"

# Check if the folder exists before proceeding
if (!dir.exists(folder_path)) {
  stop(paste("Error: The folder '", folder_path, "' does not exist. Please check the path."))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Find all Excel files
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# List all files ending with .xlsx or .xls (case-insensitive)
excel_files <- list.files(
  path = folder_path,
  pattern = "\\.(xlsx|xls)$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

# Check if any files were found
if (length(excel_files) == 0) {
  message(paste("No Excel files found in:", folder_path))
} else {
  message(paste(length(excel_files), "Excel files found. Starting conversion..."))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Loop through files and sheets
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Iterate over each Excel file path
for (file_path in excel_files) {

  # Extract the base filename (e.g., "my_data_file.xlsx")
  file_name_full <- basename(file_path)

  # Remove the extension to get the base name (e.g., "my_data_file")
  file_name_base <- sub("\\.(xlsx|xls)$", "", file_name_full, ignore.case = TRUE)

  # Clean the base name for R variable use:
  # 1. Replace any non-alphanumeric characters (including spaces, hyphens) with underscores.
  clean_file_name <- str_replace_all(file_name_base, "[^[:alnum:]_]", "_")
  # 2. Replace multiple underscores with a single underscore.
  clean_file_name <- str_replace_all(clean_file_name, "_+", "_")
  # 3. Remove leading and trailing underscores using regex replacement.
  clean_file_name <- str_replace_all(clean_file_name, "^_+|_+$", "")

  # Extract the year (four digits) from the clean file name
  # Using str_extract to get a single string result for the year
  year_match <- str_extract(clean_file_name, "\\d{4}")
  
  # Set the year value, defaulting to 'Unknown' if no four-digit pattern is found
  year_to_add <- ifelse(is.na(year_match), "UnknownYear", year_match)

  # Get the names of all sheets in the current file
  sheets <- excel_sheets(file_path)

  message(paste("Processing file:", file_name_full, "with", length(sheets), "sheets."))

  # Iterate over each sheet name
  for (sheet_name in sheets) {

    # Clean the sheet name for R variable use (similar logic as filename)
    clean_sheet_name <- str_replace_all(sheet_name, "[^[:alnum:]_]", "_")
    clean_sheet_name <- str_replace_all(clean_sheet_name, "_+", "_")
    # Remove leading and trailing underscores using regex replacement.
    clean_sheet_name <- str_replace_all(clean_sheet_name, "^_+|_+$", "")

    # Construct the final dataframe name: filename_tabname
    df_name <- paste0(clean_file_name, "_", clean_sheet_name)

    # Read the sheet data into a temporary dataframe
    # The 'col_names = TRUE' assumes the first row is the header
    tryCatch({
      data_frame <- read_excel(
        path = file_path,
        sheet = sheet_name,
        col_names = TRUE
      )
      
      # Add the extracted year as a new column for record-keeping
      data_frame$Year <- year_to_add
      
      # --- Start Column Renaming Logic ---
      # need to list here all names of columns that need to be converted to UnitName
      columns_to_rename_to_Unit_name <- 
        c(
          "Place of birth name",
          "Placeofbirthname",
          "Provider Name",
          "Provider name",
          "ProviderName",
          "Providername",
          "Provider at 48 hours",
          "Providerat48hours",
          "Hospital of final discharge",
          "Hospitaloffinaldischarge",
          "Unit name",
          "Unitname",
          "UnitName",
          " UnitName",
          ".UnitName",
          "Name"
        )
      
      data_frame <- data_frame %>%
        rename(Unit_name = any_of(columns_to_rename_to_Unit_name))
      
      if ("Unit_name" %in% names(data_frame)) {
        
        # Trim leading/trailing spaces
        data_frame$Unit_name <- trimws(data_frame$Unit_name) 
        #remove all spaces
        data_frame$Unit_name <- gsub(" ", "", data_frame$Unit_name) 
        data_frame$` UnitName` <- data_frame$Unit_name 
        
        # Replace & with AND
        data_frame$Unit_name <- gsub("&", "AND", data_frame$Unit_name)
        data_frame$Unit_name <- gsub("[()]", "", data_frame$Unit_name)
        
        
        if ("Place of birth level" %in% names(data_frame)) {
          data_frame$Unit_name <-
            paste0(data_frame$Unit_name, "_", data_frame$`Place of birth level`)
        }
        if ("Provider level" %in% names(data_frame)) {
          data_frame$Unit_name <-
            paste0(data_frame$Unit_name, "_", data_frame$`Provider level`)
        }
        

      }

      
      #get rid of any spaces and insert an underscore
      names(data_frame) <- gsub(" ", "_", names(data_frame))
      
      
      # 1. Define columns to keep unchanged (key identifiers and the new 'Year' column)
      # Ensure "Unit_name" and "Year" are always in the exclusion list as requested
      columns_to_exclude <- 
        c("Unit_name",  
          "Year")
      
      # 2. Get all current column names
      current_cols <- names(data_frame)
      
      # 3. Identify the columns that *should* be renamed (those NOT in the exclusion list)
      cols_to_rename <- current_cols[!(current_cols %in% columns_to_exclude)]
      
      # 4. Define the suffix (using the clean sheet name, preceded by an underscore)
      sheet_suffix <- paste0("_", clean_sheet_name)
      
      # 5. Create the new names for the columns that should be renamed
      # New name = original column name + sheet_suffix 
      new_names <- paste0(cols_to_rename, sheet_suffix)
      
      # 6. Apply the new names to the dataframe's column list
      # The 'match' function is used to find the positions of the columns being renamed.
      names(data_frame)[match(cols_to_rename, current_cols)] <- new_names
      
      if ("Unit_name" %in% names(data_frame)) { #only do the following if the Unit_name column exists
      #manually adjust the Unit_name column to get rid of all of the spaces, punctuation and make it capital letters
      data_frame$Unit_name <- 
        toupper(
          gsub("[[:space:][:punct:]]", "", data_frame$Unit_name))
      }
      
      # --- End Column Renaming Logic ---

      # Assign the temporary dataframe to the dynamically generated name in the global environment
      assign(df_name, data_frame, envir = .GlobalEnv)

      message(paste("  -> Successfully created dataframe:", df_name))

    }, error = function(e) {
      warning(paste("  -> Skipping sheet '", sheet_name, "' due to error:", e$message))
    })
  }
}

message("\nConversion complete.")
```
**********************************************************************************************************
Extract the level of the unit
*********************************************************************************************************************************************
```{r, 2017 unit level}
nnap_2017_unit_level <-
  data.frame(
    
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$Unit_name,
    Unit_level_name=
      as.character(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$Place_of_birth_level_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia)
  )

nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level <-
  ifelse(nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level_name=="SCU", 1, NA)
nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level <-
  ifelse(nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level_name=="LNU", 2, nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level)
nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level <-
  ifelse(nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level_name=="NICU", 3, nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level)

nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level_name <- NULL

#GLANCLWYDHOSPITALNICU is corrected to a level 2 unit, as this was level 2 in 2017
nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level <- 
  ifelse(
    nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_name=="GLANCLWYDHOSPITALNICU",
    "2",
    nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level)

#bcuhb.nhs.wales annual reports confirms this was level 2 unit"

#RAIGMOREHOSPITALINVERNESSNICU is corrected to a level 2 unit

nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level <- 
  ifelse(
    nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_name=="RAIGMOREHOSPITALINVERNESSNICU",
    "2",
    nnap_2017_unit_level$Unit_level)

#NHS Ayrshire and Arran contains university hospital crosshouse, which did used to be a level 3 unit in 2017, and therefore doesn't need manual adjustment, but was downgraded to level 2 after 2018

#NHS Fife does have Victoria hospital in kirkcaldy, which used to be a level 3 unit, and was downgraded to level 2 after 2018

#North tees and hartlepool trust used to have a level 3 unit, but then after 2015 cqc inspection, they started the process of downgrade, and by 2018 babies would be transferred to James cook hospital
```

```{r, 2018 unit level}
nnap_2018_unit_level <-
  data.frame(

#"The unit at North Tees started downgrading from level 3 care to level 1 care after the 2015 review and the noernet.org.uk network patient pathways in 2017 stated that all level 3 was from then on to be managed at James cook, which is part of the south tees trust. We therefore reassign the NNAP data for 2018 for UNIVERSITYHOSPITALOFNORTHTEES to level 1 instead of level 3"

nnap_2018_unit_level$Unit_level <- 
  ifelse(
    nnap_2018_unit_level$Unit_name=="UNIVERSITYHOSPITALOFNORTHTEES",
    "1",
    nnap_2018_unit_level$Unit_level)
```

```{r, 2022 unit level}
nnap_2022_unit_level <- data.frame(
  Unit_name = nnap_2022_data_0_BPD$Unit_name,

  row.names = NULL
)

nnap_2022_unit_level <- nnap_2022_unit_level %>%

    )
  )
```

*******************************************************************************************************
Extract the BPD data for each year first
*******************************************************************************************************

BPD is clearly split into none, mild, significant or died of bronchopulmonary dysplasia

```{r, 2017 bpd}
nnap_2017_bpd_workings <-
  data.frame(
    
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$Unit_name,
    bpd_n_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`Number_of_eligible_babies_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`),

    bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_alive=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`With_outcome_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`),
    bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`Missing_number_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`),
    bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_died=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`Died_number_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`),

    bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`No_BPD_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`),
    bpd_n_mild_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`Mild_BPD_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`),
    bpd_n_significant_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia$`Significant_BPD_number_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia`)
)

nnap_2017_bpd_workings$check_missing <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_eligible) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_alive) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data) -
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_died) 

print("This number being zero means we have the number eligible, the number with data, the number missing data AND the number died who create that eligibility:")
sum(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$check_missing, na.rm=T)

print("Number_of_eligible_babies_Bronchopulmonary_dysplasia is the number of babies born below 32 weeks gestation. This includes babies who died. We therefore need to create our own metric of how many babies were alive and eligible for the bpd metric")
nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpn_n_alive_and_eligible <-
  nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_eligible - nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_died

nnap_2017_bpd_workings$check_bpd_severity <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_alive) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_mild_bpd) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_significant_bpd) 

print("This number being zero tells us that bpd_n_with_data_and_alive comprises those with categoris of no bpd, mild bpd and significant bpd. This shows the total number of babies with bpd at each centre needs to be calculated by adding the number that died wtih bpd when it comes to 2017. ")
sum(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$check_bpd_severity, na.rm=T)

print("We therefore need to create ourself the number with any bpd. We also can go back to data if we care about death or bpd as there are other columns. 2018 doesnt have mild or severe bpd so we concatenate here and get rid of these columns")

print("All patients who had bpd are therefore no_bpd, mild_bpd, significant_bpd AND bpd_n_with_bpd_data_and_died")
nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd <-
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_mild_bpd) +
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_significant_bpd) 

print("For BPD we don't know the number of patients that died and didn't have BPD. Therefore we need to take BPD as the number of patients that were alive as the denonimator")

#now get rid of columns we don't want by creating nnap_2017_bpd
nnap_2017_bpd <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_bpd_workings$Unit_name,
    bpn_n_alive_and_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpn_n_alive_and_eligible),
    bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd),
    bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd),
    bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data)
  )

print("final check, this should be zero:")
  sum(
    (nnap_2017_bpd$bpn_n_alive_and_eligible) - 
    (nnap_2017_bpd$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd) -
    (nnap_2017_bpd$bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd) -
    (nnap_2017_bpd$bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data),
    na.rm=T
  )
  
```

```{r, 2024 bpd}
nnap_2024_bpd_workings <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Unit_name,
    
    bpd_n_alive_and_dead_eligible_for_bpd_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Eligible_BPD),
    
    bpd_n_that_had_bpd_or_died=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$BPD_or_death_BPD),

    bpd_n_alive_and_dead_with_bpd_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Outcome_BPD),
    
    bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Missing_BPD),
    
    bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$BPD_only_BPD)
)

#this is different to 2023 - we have to create those that don't have BPD by taking it from those that have data
print("This being zero tells us that the number missing plus the number with the outcome is the total number eligible")
sum(as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Eligible_BPD) -
  as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Outcome_BPD) -
  as.numeric(nnap_2024_data_report_09102025_BPD$Missing_BPD), na.rm=T )

print("We create the number that died by subtracting the number with bpd only from the number with bpd or death")
nnap_2024_bpd_workings$died_and_eligible_for_BPD_data <-
  nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_that_had_bpd_or_died - nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd

print("We create the number alive and eligible by subtracting the number that died and were eligible from the total number eligible")
nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpn_n_alive_and_eligible <-
  nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_dead_eligible_for_bpd_data - nnap_2024_bpd_workings$died_and_eligible_for_BPD_data
  
print("Therefore we can create the number alive without BPD by subtracting the number with BPD and alive and the number that died from the number with the outcome")
nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_without_any_bpd_no <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_dead_with_bpd_data) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$died_and_eligible_for_BPD_data) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd)


nnap_2024_bpd <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2024_bpd_workings$Unit_name,
    bpn_n_alive_and_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpn_n_alive_and_eligible),
    bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd),
    bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_without_any_bpd_no),
    bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2024_bpd_workings$bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data)
  )

print("final check, this should be zero:")
  sum(
    (nnap_2024_bpd$bpn_n_alive_and_eligible) - 
    (nnap_2024_bpd$bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd) -
    (nnap_2024_bpd$bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd) -
    (nnap_2024_bpd$bpd_n_alive_and_missing_bpd_data),
    na.rm=T
  )

```

```{r, 2017 NEC}
nnap_2017_NEC_workings <-
  data.frame(
    
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Unit_name,
    NEC_n_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Number_of_eligible_babies_Necrotising_enterocolitis),
    NEC_n_with_NEC_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$With_outcome_Necrotising_enterocolitis),
    NEC_n_alive_and_missing_NEC_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Missing_alive_number_Necrotising_enterocolitis),
    NEC_n_dead_and_missing_NEC_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Missing_died_number_Necrotising_enterocolitis),
    NEC_n_with_NEC_data_no_and_died_of_something_else=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Died_prior_to_discharge_home_but_had_no_NEC_Necrotising_enterocolitis),
    
    NEC_n_NEC_yes=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$NEC_number_Necrotising_enterocolitis),
    NEC_n_alive_and_NEC_no=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$No_NEC_Necrotising_enterocolitis)
)

#add the number alive without NEC and the number dead without NEC to get the total number without NEC
nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_NEC_no <-
  nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_with_NEC_data_no_and_died_of_something_else +
  nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_alive_and_NEC_no

nnap_2017_NEC_workings$check_missing <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Number_of_eligible_babies_Necrotising_enterocolitis) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$With_outcome_Necrotising_enterocolitis) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Missing_alive_number_Necrotising_enterocolitis) -
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Necrotising_enterocolitis$Missing_died_number_Necrotising_enterocolitis) 

print("This number being zero means those with missing NEC data are divided into those that are alive and those that have died and will need combining:")
sum(nnap_2017_NEC_workings$check_missing, na.rm=T)

nnap_2017_NEC_workings$missing_NEC_data <-
  nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_alive_and_missing_NEC_data + nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_dead_and_missing_NEC_data

nnap_2017_NEC <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_NEC_workings$Unit_name,
    NEC_n_alive_and_dead_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_eligible),
    NEC_n_yes_NEC=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_NEC_yes),
    NEC_n_no_NEC=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_NEC_workings$NEC_n_NEC_no),
    NEC_n_missing_NEC_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_NEC_workings$missing_NEC_data)
 )

print("final check, this should be zero:")
  sum(
    (nnap_2017_NEC$NEC_n_alive_and_dead_eligible) - 
    (nnap_2017_NEC$NEC_n_yes_NEC) -
    (nnap_2017_NEC$NEC_n_no_NEC) -
    (nnap_2017_NEC$NEC_n_missing_NEC_data),
    na.rm=T
  )
  
```

**************************
Extract the sepsis data for each year
**************************

```{r, 2017 sepsis}
#for sepsis, we need to split the file into <32 and >=32
nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_less_than_32 <-
  subset(nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection, Gestation_weeks_Bloodstream_infection=="< 32 weeks")
nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_greater_equal_32 <-
  subset(nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection, Gestation_weeks_Bloodstream_infection==">= 32 weeks")

nnap_2017_sepsis_workings <-
  data.frame(
    
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_less_than_32$Unit_name,
    
    sepsis_n_eligible_less_than_32=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_less_than_32$Number_of_babies_admitted_Bloodstream_infection),
    
    sepsis_n_with_sepsis_less_than_32_yes=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_less_than_32$Babies_with_one_or_more_pure_growths_of_a_pathogen_Bloodstream_infection),
    
    Unit_name_check=
      nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_greater_equal_32$Unit_name,
    
    sepsis_n_eligible_greater_than_32=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_greater_equal_32$Number_of_babies_admitted_Bloodstream_infection),
    
    sepsis_n_with_sepsis_greater_than_32_yes=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Bloodstream_infection_greater_equal_32$Babies_with_one_or_more_pure_growths_of_a_pathogen_Bloodstream_infection)
)

nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$different <- 
  nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$Unit_name != 
  nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$Unit_name_check
print("This tell us I haven't inadvertently combined different units if it is zero:")
sum(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$different)

print("Create the total number with sepsis by adding less than and greater than 32")
nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible_less_than_32) +
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible_greater_than_32)

nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_yes <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_less_than_32_yes) +
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_greater_than_32_yes)

nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_without_sepsis_no <- 
  nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible - 
  nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_yes

#now get rid of columns we don't want by creating nnap_2017_sepsis
nnap_2017_sepsis <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$Unit_name,
    sepsis_n_alive_and_dead_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible),
    sepsis_n_yes_sepsis=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_yes),
    sepsis_n_no_sepsis=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_without_sepsis_no),
    sepsis_n_missing_sepsis_data=
      as.numeric(NA) #kept a column just to remind us that there is no such thing as reliable missing data metric for sepsis because of the way documentation is carried out
  )

print("final check, this should be zero:")
  sum(
    (nnap_2017_sepsis$sepsis_n_alive_and_dead_eligible) - 
    (nnap_2017_sepsis$sepsis_n_yes_sepsis) -
    (nnap_2017_sepsis$sepsis_n_no_sepsis) -
    (nnap_2017_sepsis$sepsis_n_missing_sepsis_data),
    na.rm=T
  )
```

```{r, 2021 sepsis}
#In 2021, the denonimator they use to define percentages is BabiesAdmitted, they just split this into LT32 which is less than 32 and GT which is greater than 32. A positive result is reflected in the purepathogens column. We therefore have to add up LT32 and GT32")

nnap_2021_sepsis_workings <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2021_data_BSI$Unit_name,
    
    sepsis_n_eligible_less_than_32=
      as.numeric(nnap_2021_data_BSI$Number_of_babies_admitted_Less_than_32_weeks_gestation_at_birth_BSI),
    
    sepsis_n_with_sepsis_less_than_32_yes=
      as.numeric(
        sub(" .*", "", nnap_2021_data_BSI$Number_of_babies_with_one_or_more_growths_of_a_clearly_pathogenic_organism...6_BSI)
        ),

    sepsis_n_eligible_greater_than_32=
       as.numeric(nnap_2021_data_BSI$Number_of_babies_admitted_Greater_than_or_equal_to_32_weeks_gestation_at_birth_BSI),
    
    sepsis_n_with_sepsis_greater_than_32_yes=
      as.numeric(
        sub(" .*", "", nnap_2021_data_BSI$Number_of_babies_with_one_or_more_growths_of_a_clearly_pathogenic_organism...10_BSI)
        )
    )


#Create the total number with sepsis by adding less than and greater than 32
nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible_less_than_32) +
  as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible_greater_than_32)

nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_yes <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_less_than_32_yes) +
  as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_greater_than_32_yes)

nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_without_sepsis_no <- 
  nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible - 
  nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_yes

nnap_2021_sepsis <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$Unit_name,
    sepsis_n_alive_and_dead_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_eligible),
    sepsis_n_yes_sepsis=
      as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_with_sepsis_yes),
    sepsis_n_no_sepsis=
      as.numeric(nnap_2021_sepsis_workings$sepsis_n_without_sepsis_no),
    sepsis_n_missing_sepsis_data=
      as.numeric(NA) #kept a column just to remind us that there is no such thing as reliable missing data metric for sepsis because of the way it is done
  )

print("final check, this should be zero:")
  sum(
    (nnap_2021_sepsis$sepsis_n_alive_and_dead_eligible) - 
    (nnap_2021_sepsis$sepsis_n_yes_sepsis) -
    (nnap_2021_sepsis$sepsis_n_no_sepsis) -
    (nnap_2021_sepsis$sepsis_n_missing_sepsis_data),
    na.rm=T
  )

```

******************************************************************************************
temperature at admission normothermia
*****************************************************


```{r, 2017 Temperature}
nnap_2017_Temperature_workings <-
  data.frame(
    
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$Unit_name,
    Temperature_n_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$Eligible_babies_Temperature),
    Temperature_n_with_Temperature_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$With_outcome_Temperature),

    Temperature_n_normothermia_yes=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$`Temp._36.5_to_37.5°C_number_Temperature`),
    
    Temperature_n_Temperature_low=
      as.numeric(
        nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$`Temp._less_than_32°C_Temperature` +
        nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$`Temp._32_to_35.9°C_Temperature` +
        nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$`Temp._36_to_36.4°C_number_Temperature` 
        ),
    
    Temperature_n_Temperature_high=
      as.numeric(
        nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$`Temp._greater_than_37.5°C_number_Temperature`
        )
)

#calculate missing by adding the number missing and the number not taken and the number taken after an hour
nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_missing <-
  nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$Not_taken_Temperature +
  nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$After_hour_Temperature +
  nnap_2017_data_0_Temperature$Missing_data_number_Temperature

nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$check_missing <- 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_eligible) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_low) - 
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_high) -
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_normothermia_yes) -
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_missing) 

print("This number being zero means those with missing Temperature data are divided into those that are alive and those that have died and will need combining:")
sum(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$check_missing, na.rm=T)

#we now create normothermia no by adding all of the numbers that are low or high
nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_normothermia_no <-
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_low) +
  as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_high)

#now get rid of columns we don't want by creating nnap_2017_Temperature
nnap_2017_Temperature <-
  data.frame(
    Unit_name=
      nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Unit_name,
    Temperature_n_eligible=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_eligible),
    Temperature_n_normothermia_yes=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_normothermia_yes),
    Temperature_n_normothermia_no=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_normothermia_no),
    Temperature_n_Temperature_low=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_low),
    Temperature_n_Temperature_high=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_high),
    Temperature_n_missing_Temperature_data=
      as.numeric(nnap_2017_Temperature_workings$Temperature_n_Temperature_missing)
 )

print("final check, this should be zero:")
  sum(
    (nnap_2017_Temperature$Temperature_n_eligible) - 
    (nnap_2017_Temperature$Temperature_n_Temperature_yes) -
    (nnap_2017_Temperature$Temperature_n_Temperature_no) -
    (nnap_2017_Temperature$Temperature_n_Temperature_missing),
    na.rm=T
  )
#this is working
```

```{r, helper function to combine all metrics into one frame for one year}
combine_nnap_data_for_same_year <- function(year) {
  
  level <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_unit_level"))
  
  
  bpd   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_bpd"))
  NEC   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_NEC"))
  sepsis<- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_sepsis"))
  IVH   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_IVH"))
  cPVL  <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_cPVL"))
  DCC   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_DCC"))
  ANS   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_ANS"))
  MgSO   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_MgSO"))
  temp   <- get(paste0("nnap_", year, "_Temperature"))
  
  #join each of those in turn to our 
  all_nnap_data_for_year <-
    level %>%
    full_join(bpd,    by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(NEC,    by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(sepsis, by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(IVH,    by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(cPVL,   by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(DCC,    by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(ANS,    by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(MgSO,   by = join_by(Unit_name)) %>%
    full_join(temp,   by = join_by(Unit_name))
  
  #then we join our manual unit levels  
  manual_unit_levels <- 
    read.csv("manual_unit_level_definition/NNAP_manual_unit_levels_to_add.csv")
  
  #in each level frame for the year, we add in our manual frame
  all_nnap_data_for_year_with_manual_unit_level <- 
    left_join(all_nnap_data_for_year, manual_unit_levels, by = "Unit_name")
  
  #use the manual unit level if we don't have a unit level in the frame from NNAP
  # use manual unit level if missing in NNAP data
  all_nnap_data_for_year_with_manual_unit_level <- 
    all_nnap_data_for_year_with_manual_unit_level %>%
    mutate(Unit_level = ifelse(is.na(Unit_level), Unit_level_manual, Unit_level))
}

# loop through years and assign merged dataframes
for (yr in 2017:2024) {
  merged <- combine_nnap_data_for_same_year(yr)
  assign(paste0("nnap_", yr), merged)
}
```

load MBRRACE data

```{r, load all the MBRRACE data frames of total mortality data and modernise the trust names}
#When we load MBRRACE data frames, we change any hospital trust names that have been updated, or trusts that have been merged. So all trust names in our version of the MBRRACE data are the most recent trust names
# We use 'stringr' for file/name manipulation and base R's 'read.csv' for loading data.
library(stringr) # For easy string manipulation (cleaning file names)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Configuration
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Define the folder containing the CSV files
folder_path <- "MBRRACE_raw_data/total_mortality"

# Check if the folder exists before proceeding
if (!dir.exists(folder_path)) {
  stop(paste("Error: The folder '", folder_path, "' does not exist. Please check the path."))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Find all CSV files
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# List all files ending with .csv (case-insensitive)
# We are now looking for CSV files only.
csv_files <- list.files(
  path = folder_path,
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

# Check if any files were found
if (length(csv_files) == 0) {
  message(paste("No CSV files found in:", folder_path))
} else {
  message(paste(length(csv_files), "CSV files found. Starting conversion..."))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Loop through files
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Iterate over each CSV file path
for (file_path in csv_files) {

  # Extract the base filename (e.g., "MBRRACE_2020.csv")
  file_name_full <- basename(file_path)

  # Remove the extension to get the base name (e.g., "MBRRACE_2020")
  file_name_base <- sub("\\.csv$", "", file_name_full, ignore.case = TRUE)

  # Clean the base name for R variable use:
  # 1. Replace any non-alphanumeric characters (including spaces, hyphens) with underscores.
  clean_file_name <- str_replace_all(file_name_base, "[^[:alnum:]_]", "_")
  # 2. Replace multiple underscores with a single underscore.
  clean_file_name <- str_replace_all(clean_file_name, "_+", "_")
  # 3. Remove leading and trailing underscores using regex replacement.
  clean_file_name <- str_replace_all(clean_file_name, "^_+|_+$", "")

  # Extract the year (four digits) from the clean file name
  # We use str_extract (singular) to get a single character string match.
  year_match <- str_extract(clean_file_name, "\\d{4}")
  
  # Set the year value, defaulting to 'Unknown' if no four-digit pattern is found
  year_to_add <- ifelse(is.na(year_match), "UnknownYear", year_match)

  # The dataframe name is now just the cleaned filename, as CSVs don't have tabs
  df_name <- clean_file_name

  message(paste("Processing file:", file_name_full, "-> Target DF:", df_name))

  # Read the CSV data into a temporary dataframe
  # Uses base R's read.csv function, assuming comma separation.
  tryCatch({
    data_frame <- read.csv(
      file = file_path,
      header = TRUE, # Assumes first row is the header
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE # Recommended practice to prevent character data being converted to factors
    )

          if ("OrganisationName" %in% names(data_frame)) { #only do the following if the Unit_name column exists
      #manually adjust the Unit_name column to get rid of all of the spaces, punctuation and make it capital letters
      data_frame$OrganisationName <- 
        toupper(
          gsub("[[:space:][:punct:]]", "", data_frame$OrganisationName))
          }
    
        # Replace & with AND
        data_frame$OrganisationName <- gsub("&", "AND", data_frame$OrganisationName)
        data_frame$OrganisationName <- gsub("[()]", "", data_frame$OrganisationName)
    
    data_frame <- data_frame %>%
        rename(Trust_name = OrganisationName)
    
    #now we do manual changes to the MBRRACE data sheets to reflect the modern trust names
    #in our linkage sheet, we only have one trust name
    #in our linkage sheets, we can have multiple hospital names, but these only link to one trust, and therefore when we join trusts to hospitals, we don't get any many to one joins. You would do if you ever went the other way, but we don't want to, we want to combine NNAP data into trusts
    #the linkage spreadsheet has some hospital names as NO_NNAP_HOSPITAL data for places like the shetlands and for belfast (Northern ireland), which means that MBRRACE trust data will not be linked to any hospital
    
    #IMPORTANT: before the ifelse statements to adjust trust name, we pull out Trust_name_original. This will allow us to flag trusts that have at times along the way been concatenated
    data_frame$Trust_name_original <- data_frame$Trust_name
    
    #YEOVILDISTRICTHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST update to SOMERSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
      data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="YEOVILDISTRICTHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "SOMERSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name) 

    #Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust: trust details and documents. This trust was formerly known as Homerton University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust.
#HOMERTONUNIVERSITYHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST needs updating to HOMERTONHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
      
      data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="HOMERTONUNIVERSITYHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "HOMERTONHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)  
      
      #Luton and Dunstable University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust was an NHS foundation trust which ran Luton and Dunstable University Hospital. The trust acquired Bedford Hospital NHS Trust on 1 April 2020, forming Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.
      
#      LUTONANDDUNSTABLEUNIVERSITYHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST updating to BEDFORDSHIREHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
            data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="BEDFORDHOSPITALNHSTRUST",
        "BEDFORDSHIREHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)  
            data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="LUTONANDDUNSTABLEUNIVERSITYHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "BEDFORDSHIREHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)  
            
            #THEPENNINEACUTEHOSPITALSNHSTRUST to NORTHERNCAREALLIANCENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
                        data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="THEPENNINEACUTEHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "NORTHERNCAREALLIANCENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name) 
                        
            #TAUNTONANDSOMERSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST to SOMERSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
                        data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="TAUNTONANDSOMERSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "SOMERSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name) 
            
 #"EASTSUFFOLKANDNORTHESSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST was formed on 1 July 2018 through the merger of Colchester Hospital University NHS Foundation Trust and The Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust."
                        
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="COLCHESTERHOSPITALUNIVERSITYNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "EASTSUFFOLKANDNORTHESSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="THEIPSWICHHOSPITALNHSTRUST",
        "EASTSUFFOLKANDNORTHESSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #In July 2018 Burton Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust was part of a merger with Derby Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, which created the University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust and Burton Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust ceased to exist.
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="BURTONHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSOFDERBYANDBURTONNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    #simple name change of lewisham
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="LEWISHAMANDGREENWICHNHSTRUST",
        "LEWISHAMANDGREENWICHNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #A merger with Basildon and Thurrock University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and Southend University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust was proposed in January 2018.[2] On 31 July 2019 the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care endorsed the merger and a provisional date of 1 April 2020 was agreed.
    #SOUTHENDUNIVERSITYHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST needs changing to  MIDANDSOUTHESSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="MIDESSEXHOSPITALSERVICESNHSTRUST",
        "MIDANDSOUTHESSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SOUTHENDUNIVERSITYHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "MIDANDSOUTHESSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #It was announced in January 2018 that the Trust would be changing its name to University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust. This was to reflect its collaboration with University of Plymouth and with the Plymouth University Peninsula Schools of Medicine and Dentistry.
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="PLYMOUTHHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSPLYMOUTHNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #merger for name change of SOUTHDEVONHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST to TORBAYANDSOUTHDEVONNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SOUTHDEVONHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "TORBAYANDSOUTHDEVONNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #NORTHERNDEVONHEALTHCARENHSTRUST and ROYALDEVONANDEXETERNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST needs changing to ROYALDEVONUNIVERSITYHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="NORTHERNDEVONHEALTHCARENHSTRUST",
        "ROYALDEVONUNIVERSITYHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="ROYALDEVONANDEXETERNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "ROYALDEVONUNIVERSITYHEALTHCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    #Western Sussex Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust was an NHS foundation trust which ran Worthing Hospital, Southlands Hospital in Shoreham-by-Sea and St Richard's Hospital in Chichester, West Sussex, England and served a population of around 450,000 people across a catchment area covering most of West Sussex. It was formed through a merger in 2009 and started with a substantial inherited deficit, mortality issues and poor performance. It merged into University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust in 2021.
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="WESTERNSUSSEXHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSSUSSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    #The trust was established on 1 April 2021 following the merger of Brighton and Sussex University Hospitals NHS Trust and Western Sussex Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="BRIGHTONANDSUSSEXUNIVERSITYHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSSUSSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="WARRINGTONANDHALTONHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "WARRINGTONANDHALTONTEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #2017 heart of england trust doesn't exist anymore, it has been taken over by, Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="HEARTOFENGLANDNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "BIRMINGHAMWOMENSANDCHILDRENSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #On 1 March 2019, NHS Improvement was notified of the trust name change from Hull and East Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust to Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust.
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="HULLANDEASTYORKSHIREHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "HULLUNIVERSITYTEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #manx care was establish in April 2021 from the isle of man department of health and social care
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="ISLEOFMANDEPARTMENTOFHEALTHANDSOCIALCARE",
        "MANXCARE",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #To reflect the change in approach, the trust's name was changed in 2016 from Tameside Hospital NHS Foundation Trust to Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="TAMESIDEHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "TAMESIDEANDGLOSSOPINTEGRATEDCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #It agreed in July 2015 to join the Black Country Alliance with Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust and Walsall Healthcare NHS Trust. THEDUDLEYGROUPNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST to SANDWELLANDWESTBIRMINGHAMHOSPITALSNHSTRUST
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="THEDUDLEYGROUPNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "SANDWELLANDWESTBIRMINGHAMHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    #On the 1 July 2023 Southport and Ormskirk Hospital NHS Trust was dissolved and its staff, property, services and liabilities were transferred to St Helens and Knowsley Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust. At this time the trusts name was changed to Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust.
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="STHELENSANDKNOWSLEYTEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "MERSEYANDWESTLANCASHIRETEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SOUTHPORTANDORMSKIRKHOSPITALNHSTRUST",
        "MERSEYANDWESTLANCASHIRETEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SOUTHPORTORMSKIRKHOSPITALNHSTRUST",
        "MERSEYANDWESTLANCASHIRETEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SOUTHWARWICKSHIRENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "SOUTHWARWICKSHIREUNIVERSITYNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #modernised name only for WESTHERTFORDSHIRETEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="WESTHERTFORDSHIREHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "WESTHERTFORDSHIRETEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust was created in October 2019 by a merger between Cumbria Partnership NHS Foundation Trust and North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="NORTHCUMBRIAUNIVERSITYHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "NORTHCUMBRIAINTEGRATEDCARENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust and Solent NHS Trust have merged to form the new NHS Trust, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare
    #isle of wight trust is the name used in MBRRACE thouse so no change necessary to this new name

    #The South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust was formed on April 1, 2019, through the merger of City Hospitals Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust and South Tyneside NHS Foundation Trust

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SOUTHTYNESIDENHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "SOUTHTYNESIDEANDSUNDERLANDNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="CITYHOSPITALSSUNDERLANDNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "SOUTHTYNESIDEANDSUNDERLANDNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #In February 2019 it was decided to rename it Swansea Bay University Health Board and to alter the boundary with the Cwm Taf University Health Board (now Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board)

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="ABERTAWEBROMORGANNWGUNIVERSITYHEALTHBOARD",
        "CWMTAFMORGANNWGUNIVERSITYHEALTHBOARD",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="SWANSEABAYUNIVERSITYHEALTHBOARD",
        "CWMTAFMORGANNWGUNIVERSITYHEALTHBOARD",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #simple rename of portsmouth

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="PORTSMOUTHHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "PORTSMOUTHHOSPITALSUNIVERSITYNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
        #It was renamed from Cwm Taf University Health Board on 1 April 2019 following the transfer of Bridgend County Borough from the former Abertawe Bro Morgannwg University Health Board (now Swansea Bay University Health Board).
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="CWMTAFUNIVERSITYHEALTHBOARD",
        "CWMTAFMORGANNWGUNIVERSITYHEALTHBOARD",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #The Royal Bournemouth Hospital is an acute general hospital in Bournemouth, Dorset, England. It is managed by the University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust. The hospital was managed by The Royal Bournemouth and Christchurch Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust until the merger with Poole Hospital NHS Foundation Trust on 1 October 2020.
#POOLEHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST to UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSDORSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="THEROYALBOURNEMOUTHANDCHRISTCHURCHHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATION",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSDORSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="POOLEHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSDORSETNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust was established in 2024 to bring health and care services closer together for local people
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="KINGSTONHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "KINGSTONANDRICHMONDNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)    
    
#United Lincolnshire Hospitals NHS Trust announced on 16 September 2024 that it had been awarded teaching-hospital status by the Secretary of State
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="UNITEDLINCOLNSHIREHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "UNITEDLINCOLNSHIRETEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)      
    
#Oxford university hospitals NHS trust became oxford university hospitals NHS foundation trust in 2024
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="OXFORDUNIVERSITYHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "OXFORDUNIVERSITYHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)        

#Whittington has been an NHS trust in the name since 2017, but the MBRRACE name only became this later on, the name just needs to be made consistent

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="WHITTINGTONHEALTH",
        "WHITTINGTONHEALTHNHSTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)        
    
#Wrightington wigan and leigh named itself a teaching hospital trust in 2020 and just needs to be made consistent

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="WRIGHTINGTONWIGANANDLEIGHNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "WRIGHTINGTONWIGANANDLEIGHTEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)            

    
    #UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSSUSSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST The trust was established on 1 April 2021 following the merger of Brighton and Sussex University Hospitals NHS Trust and Western Sussex Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="BRIGHTONANDSUSSEXUNIVERSITYHOSPITALSNHSTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSSUSSEXNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #The Weston Area Health NHS Trust merged with University Hospitals Bristol NHS Foundation Trust on April 1, 2020, to form the new University Hospitals Bristol and Weston NHS Foundation Trust (UHBW).

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="WESTONAREAHEALTHNHSTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSBRISTOLANDWESTONNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSBRISTOLNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "UNIVERSITYHOSPITALSBRISTOLANDWESTONNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    #TOn 1 April 2021 the trust changed its name to York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="YORKTEACHINGHOSPITALNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        "YORKANDSCARBOROUGHTEACHINGHOSPITALSNHSFOUNDATIONTRUST",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    #manual correction of an AND for NHSAYRSHIREANDARRAN
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="NHSAYRSHIREARRAN",
        "NHSAYRSHIREANDARRAN",
        data_frame$Trust_name)

    #manual correction of an AND for NHSDUMFRIESGALLOWAY
    data_frame$Trust_name <-
      ifelse(
        data_frame$Trust_name=="NHSDUMFRIESGALLOWAY",
        "NHSDUMFRIESANDGALLOWAY",
        data_frame$Trust_name)
    
    # Add the extracted year as a new column for record-keeping
    # The 'year_to_add' value is automatically recycled to match the number of rows.
    data_frame$Year <- year_to_add

    # Assign the temporary dataframe to the dynamically generated name in the global environment
    assign(df_name, data_frame, envir = .GlobalEnv)

    message(paste("  -> Successfully created dataframe:", df_name))

  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("  -> Skipping file '", file_name_full, "' due to error:", e$message))
  })
}

message("\nConversion complete.")
```


The idea here is that it is okay to have pseudonyms of hospitals in the linkage spreadsheet as they won't be joined twice, because we are left joining trusts to units, then collecting data from all rows of each trust. However one cannot have multiple trust names for the same hospital in the same linkage spreadsheet as that will then create a many to one join. Therefore all names of trusts have been standardised to their new name, to facilitate collecting all of the data on all of the years.

The key is to change names of trusts in the MBRRACE data sheets to be consistent also.

******************************************************************************
Joining MBRRACE data to NNAP data
******************************************************************************

As some trusts have merged with others, we need to combine MBRRACE data to ensure there is only one row per trust, using all the modern trusts by combining data as necessary

```{r, combine trusts as necessary and tidy the MBRRACE data frame}
#in this chunk we remove unnecessary columns from the MBRRACE data frames, so if something is missing, check what has been removed here

for (yr in 2017:2024) {
  
  all_MBRRACE_data_for_year <- 
    get(paste0("perinatal_mortality_rates_", yr, "_trusthealth_board"))

  # drop unnecessary columns in one go
  all_MBRRACE_data_for_year <- all_MBRRACE_data_for_year %>%
    select(-c(
      CrudeStillbirthCategoryName,
      StabilisedStillbirthCategoryName,
      StabilisedStillbirthCI,
      CrudeNeonatalDeathCategoryName,
      StabilisedNeonatalDeathCategoryName,
      StabilisedNeonatalDeathCI,
      CrudePerinatalDeathCategoryName,
      StabilisedPerinatalDeathCategoryName,
      StabilisedPerinatalDeathCI
    ))
  
  # define which columns to sum and which columns to take a mean when we combine trusts that have since merged
  columns_to_sum <- 
    c("TotalBirths", 
      "TotalStillbirths", 
      "TotalLiveBirths", 
      "TotalNeonatalDeaths", 
      "TotalPerinatalDeaths")

  columns_to_mean <- 
    c("Longitude", 
      "Latitude", 
      "CrudeStillbirthRate", 
      "CrudeNeonatalDeathRate", 
      "StabilisedStillbirthRate", 
      "StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate", 
      "CrudePerinatalDeathRate", 
      "StabilisedPerinatalDeathRate", 
      "CrudePerinatalDeathRate", 
      "GroupAverageStillbirthRate", 
      "GroupAverageNeonatalDeathRate", 
      "GroupAverageStillbirthRate", 
      "GroupAveragePerinatalDeathRate")

  # summarise with dynamic across()
  MBRRACE_data_for_year_trusts_combined <-
    all_MBRRACE_data_for_year %>%
    group_by(CountryName, RegionName, Trust_name) %>%
    summarise(
      ComparatorGroupID = min(ComparatorGroupID, na.rm = T),
      MBRRACE_report_year = first(ReportYear),
      NeonatalNetworkName = paste(unique(NeonatalNetworkName), collapse = "; "),
      OrganisationCode = paste(unique(OrganisationCode), collapse = "; "),
      Trust_name_original = paste(unique(Trust_name_original), collapse = "; "),
      number_of_trusts_combined = length(unique(Trust_name_original)),
      across(all_of(columns_to_mean), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "{.col}"),
      across(all_of(columns_to_sum), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "{.col}"),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  #we recreate out comparator group name from the comparator group ID
MBRRACE_data_for_year_trusts_combined <- 
  MBRRACE_data_for_year_trusts_combined %>%
  mutate(
    ComparatorGroupName = case_when(
      ComparatorGroupID == 1 ~ "Level_3_NICU_and_neonatal_surgery",
      ComparatorGroupID == 2 ~ "Level_3_NICU",
      ComparatorGroupID == 3 ~ "Over_4000_births",
      ComparatorGroupID == 4 ~ "Between_2000_3999_births",
      ComparatorGroupID == 5 ~ "Under_2000_births",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
  
  assign(
    paste0("MBRRACE_trusts_combined_", yr), 
    MBRRACE_data_for_year_trusts_combined, 
    envir = .GlobalEnv
  )
}


```

Now the linkage spreadsheet has been made consistent through iterations of this file, we can join the trust name to the NNAP data with a left_join, always ensuring we have a trust name for our NNAP data

```{r, adding a trust name to each hospital and add up all data for hospitals within trust to create NNAP data by trust for each separate year also pull out trusts without a level}
#create an empty frame to bind to 
NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level <- data.frame()
NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level <- data.frame()

#if we don't have data for one of the hospitals in the trust, then that hospital just doesn't contribute to the figures (i.e. na.rm)
for (yr in 2017:2024) {
  
  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_with_rows_of_NAs <- 
    get(paste0("nnap_", yr, "_with_trust_name"))
  
  #we can remove any rows from the NNAP data that are na, i.e. they are completely empty
  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name <-
    NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_with_rows_of_NAs %>%
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na))
  print(paste0(
    "Removed_", 
    nrow(NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_with_rows_of_NAs) - 
      nrow(NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name), 
    "_rows with NA in every column"))
  
  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name$Unit_level_number <- 
    as.numeric(NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name$Unit_level)

  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_without_unit_level <-
    subset(NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name, is.na(Unit_level_number))
  if (nrow(NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_without_unit_level)>0){
  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_without_unit_level$Year <- yr
  }
  
  NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level <- 
    bind_rows(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level,
          NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_without_unit_level)           
           
  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_with_unit_level <-
    subset(NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name, !is.na(Unit_level_number))
  NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_with_unit_level$Year <- yr
  
  
  NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level <- 
    bind_rows(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level,
          NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name_with_unit_level)           

  #collapse our NNAP data for each year so we have totals for each trust
  NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust <-
    NNAP_data_for_year_with_trust_name %>%
    filter(!is.na(Trust_name)) %>%
    group_by(Trust_name) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        Unit_names = paste(unique(Unit_name), collapse = "; "),
        Unit_levels = paste(unique(Unit_level), collapse = "; "),
        Unit_level_highest = max(Unit_level_number, na.rm=T),
        Year = yr,
        across(
        .cols = where(is.numeric),
        .fns = sum,
        na.rm = FALSE
        )
      )
  NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust$Unit_level_highest_character <-
    as.character(NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust$Unit_level_highest)
 
     #assign the data back to the environment
  assign(
    paste0("NNAP_data_for_", yr, "_by_trust"), 
    NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust, envir = .GlobalEnv)
}

#now we can print our trusts without unit levels to a file for manual addition
  dir.create("manual_unit_level_definition")      
  
  NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level <-
    unique(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level[,c("Unit_name", "Unit_level", "Year")])
  
  NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level <-
    unique(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level[,c("Unit_name", "Unit_level", "Year")])

  NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level <-
    NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level[
      order(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level$Unit_name), ]
  
  write.csv(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level,
            "manual_unit_level_definition/NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level.csv",

  write.csv(NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level,
            "manual_unit_level_definition/NNAP_data_with_trust_name_with_unit_level.csv",
            row.names=F)
#note that these unit levels will then get joined in ABOVE this point in the code, so if things are working, the created csv file should be empty with all trusts having a unit level. However, in future years have a look at this spreadsheet to see if any units need a level assigning to them
  print("check manual_unit_level_definition/NNAP_data_with_trust_name_without_unit_level.csv is EMPTY to ensure we know the level of each unit")
```

now we have totals by trust, we can calculate percentages for each of our metrics

```{r, calculating percentages of each outcome and pulling out trusts without unit levels}

for (yr in 2017:2024) {
  NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust_with_percent <- 
    get(paste0("NNAP_data_for_", yr, "_by_trust"))
  
library(dplyr)
  

NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust_with_percent <- 
  NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust_with_percent %>%
  mutate(
    
    bpd_crude_pct = if_else(
      (bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd + bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd /
        (bpd_n_alive_and_yes_bpd + bpd_n_alive_and_no_bpd) * 100
    ),
    
    NEC_crude_pct = if_else(
      (NEC_n_yes_NEC + NEC_n_no_NEC) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      NEC_n_yes_NEC / (NEC_n_yes_NEC + NEC_n_no_NEC) * 100
    ),
    
    sepsis_crude_pct = if_else(
      (sepsis_n_yes_sepsis + sepsis_n_no_sepsis) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      sepsis_n_yes_sepsis / (sepsis_n_yes_sepsis + sepsis_n_no_sepsis) * 100
    ),
    
    IVH_crude_pct = if_else(
      (IVH_n_yes_IVH + IVH_n_no_IVH) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      IVH_n_yes_IVH / (IVH_n_yes_IVH + IVH_n_no_IVH) * 100
    ),
    
    cPVL_crude_pct = if_else(
      (cPVL_n_yes_cPVL + cPVL_n_no_cPVL) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      cPVL_n_yes_cPVL / (cPVL_n_yes_cPVL + cPVL_n_no_cPVL) * 100
    ),
    
    DCC_crude_pct = if_else(
      (DCC_n_yes_DCC + DCC_n_no_DCC) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      DCC_n_yes_DCC / (DCC_n_yes_DCC + DCC_n_no_DCC) * 100
    ),
    
    ANS_crude_pct = if_else(
      (ANS_n_yes_ANS + ANS_n_no_ANS) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      ANS_n_yes_ANS / (ANS_n_yes_ANS + ANS_n_no_ANS) * 100
    ),
    
    MgSO_crude_pct = if_else(
      (MgSO_n_yes_MgSO + MgSO_n_no_MgSO) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      MgSO_n_yes_MgSO / (MgSO_n_yes_MgSO + MgSO_n_no_MgSO) * 100
    ),
    
    normothermia_crude_pct = if_else(
      (Temperature_n_normothermia_yes + Temperature_n_normothermia_no) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      Temperature_n_normothermia_yes / (Temperature_n_normothermia_yes + Temperature_n_normothermia_no) * 100
    ),
    
    hypothermia_crude_pct = if_else(
      (Temperature_n_normothermia_yes + Temperature_n_normothermia_no) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      Temperature_n_Temperature_low / (Temperature_n_normothermia_yes + Temperature_n_normothermia_no) * 100
    ),
    
    hyperthermia_crude_pct = if_else(
      (Temperature_n_normothermia_yes + Temperature_n_normothermia_no) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      Temperature_n_Temperature_high / (Temperature_n_normothermia_yes + Temperature_n_normothermia_no) * 100
    )
  )
    
  assign(
    paste0("NNAP_data_for_", yr, "_by_trust_with_percent"), 
    NNAP_data_for_year_by_trust_with_percent, envir = .GlobalEnv)
}

```

then join in our MBRRACE data, so that we can assess associations between NNAP percentages and MBRRACE outcome figures

```{r, join MBRRACE data to the NNAP data that has been combined into trusts to make NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data_}
all_duplicates <- list()

for (yr in 2017:2024) {
  NNAP_data_for_year <- 
    get(paste0("NNAP_data_for_", yr, "_by_trust_with_percent"))
  
# get the MBRRACE data for that year
  MBRRACE_data_for_year <- 
    get(paste0("MBRRACE_trusts_combined_", yr))
  
  #join the MBRRACE data for that year to the NNAP data
  
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data <- 
    left_join(
      NNAP_data_for_year,
      MBRRACE_data_for_year, 
      by = join_by(Trust_name))
  
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudeStillbirthRate <- 
    ifelse(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudeStillbirthRate==-1,
           NA,
           NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudeStillbirthRate)
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudeNeonatalDeathRate <- 
    ifelse(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudeNeonatalDeathRate==-1,
           NA,
           NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudeNeonatalDeathRate)
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudePerinatalDeathRate <- 
    ifelse(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudePerinatalDeathRate==-1,
           NA,
           NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data$CrudePerinatalDeathRate)
  
  #print check that we haven't had a many to many join
  print("This number should be zero, otherwise multiple trusts are getting joined to the same unit")
  print(nrow(NNAP_data_for_year) - nrow(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data))
  print("This is the number of trusts for which we have MBRRACE data but no NNAP data in this year:")
  print(nrow(MBRRACE_data_for_year) - nrow(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data))
  
  #assign the data back to the environment
  assign(
    paste0("NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data_", yr), 
    NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data, envir = .GlobalEnv)

  cat("Number of rows in combined_data_", yr, ": ", nrow(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data), "\n", sep = "")
  
  # check for duplicated Unit_names
  duplicated_units <- 
    NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data %>%
    group_by(Unit_names) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    distinct(Unit_names)
  
  if (nrow(duplicated_units) > 0) {
  all_duplicates[[as.character(yr)]] <- NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data %>%
    filter(Unit_names %in% duplicated_units$Unit_names) %>%
    select(Unit_names, Trust_name)
}
  
if (nrow(duplicated_units) > 0) {
  cat("Duplicated Unit_name(s) in combined_data_", yr, " with corresponding Trust_name(s):\n", sep = "")
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data %>%
    filter(Unit_names %in% duplicated_units$Unit_names) %>%
    select(Unit_names, Trust_name) %>%
    arrange(Unit_names) %>%
    print()
    cat("There are duplicated Unit_names in NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data for ", yr, "\n MAKE SURE YOU CHECK THEM \n", sep = "")
    cat("\n")
    
} else {
  cat("No duplicated Unit_names in combined_data_", yr, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}

    # check for duplicated Trust_name
  duplicated_trusts <- 
    NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data %>%
    group_by(Trust_name) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    distinct(Trust_name)
  
  if (nrow(duplicated_trusts) > 0) {
  all_duplicates[[as.character(yr)]] <- NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data %>%
    filter(Trust_name %in% duplicated_trusts$Trust_name) %>%
    select(Unit_names, Trust_name)
}
  
if (nrow(duplicated_trusts) > 0) {
  cat("Duplicated Trust_name(s) in combined_data_", yr, " with corresponding Trust_name(s):\n", sep = "")
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data %>%
    filter(Trust_name %in% duplicated_trusts$Trust_name) %>%
    select(Unit_names, Trust_name) %>%
    arrange(Trust_name) %>%
    print()
    cat("There are duplicated Trust_name in NNAP_and_MBRRACE_combined_data for ", yr, "\n MAKE SURE YOU CHECK THEM \n", sep = "")
    cat("\n")
    
} else {
  cat("No duplicated Trust_name in combined_data_", yr, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}
  
}

all_duplicates_df <- bind_rows(all_duplicates, .id = "Year")
```

```{r, correct MBRRACE coding of unkonwn numbers due to small number suppression to NA}
#you can have a crude neonatal death rate of -1, but a stabilised neonatal death rate that exists. THis is because of small number suppression - if there a low number of deaths the crude rate doesnt get reported, and that gets marked as -1. Therefore we change this to NA

#we change the necessary columns that have -1 or -2 to NA if we don't have the data
cols <- 
  c("TotalStillbirths", 
    "TotalPerinatalDeaths",
    "TotalLiveBirths", 
    "TotalNeonatalDeaths")

NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years[cols] <- 
  lapply(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years[cols], function(x) ifelse(x %in% c(-1, -2), NA, x))
```

```{r, function to rank both low and high being good}
library(dplyr)

rank_vars <- 
  function(
    data, 
    low_is_good, 
    high_is_good, 
    group_var = "Year") {

  data %>%
    group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
    mutate(
      # LOW → HIGH ranks, NAs stay NA
      across(all_of(low_is_good),
             ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), NA, rank(.x, ties.method = "min")),
             .names = "{.col}_rank"),
      # HIGH → LOW ranks, NAs stay NA
      across(all_of(high_is_good),
             ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), NA, rank(-.x, ties.method = "min")),
             .names = "{.col}_rank")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```

```{r, create a function to rank variables with no ties using alphabetical order for any ranks for purposes of a table}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

rank_vars_no_ties <- 
  function(
    data, 
    low_is_good, 
    high_is_good, 
    trust_var = "Trust_name",
    group_var = "Year") {

  # LOW is good
  for (v in low_is_good) {
    data <- data %>%
      group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
      arrange(.data[[v]], .data[[trust_var]], .by_group = TRUE) %>%
      mutate(
        "{v}_no_ties" := ifelse(
          is.na(.data[[v]]),
          NA_integer_,
          row_number()
        )
      ) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  # HIGH is good
  for (v in high_is_good) {
    data <- data %>%
      group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
      arrange(desc(.data[[v]]), .data[[trust_var]], .by_group = TRUE) %>%
      mutate(
        "{v}_no_ties" := ifelse(
          is.na(.data[[v]]),
          NA_integer_,
          row_number()
        )
      ) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  data
}

```

```{r, create a separate column that tells us when the rank is tied so we can mark this in the table if we want}
#helper function
flag_ties <- function(data, vars, group_var = "Year") {
  data %>%
    group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(vars),
        ~ ifelse(
          is.na(.x),
          NA_integer_,
          ave(.x, .x, FUN = length) > 1
        ) |> as.integer(),
        .names = "{.col}_is_tied"
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years_ranked <-
  flag_ties(
    data = NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years,
    vars = low_is_good_variables,
    group_var = "Year"
  )
```

```{r, min max normalisation function from 0 good to 1 bad}
library(dplyr)
NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years_ranked <- 
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years_ranked %>%
    group_by(Year) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      ends_with("_rank"),
      ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), NA, (.x - min(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) / 
                              (max(.x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(.x, na.rm = TRUE))),
      .names = "{.col}_norm"
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  )
```

```{r, min max normalisation function from 0 bad to 100 good}
library(dplyr)
NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years_ranked <- 
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_all_years_ranked %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      ends_with("_rank"),
      ~ ifelse(
          is.na(.x), 
          NA, 
          100 * (max(.x, na.rm = TRUE) - .x) /
            (max(.x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
        ),
      .names = "{.col}_percentile"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

```{r, simplify our ranks to deciles}
library(dplyr)
predictors_to_decile <- 
  c(
    "StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_rank_percentile",

    "mean_rank_percentile", 
    "mean_perinatal_rank_percentile", 
    "mean_morbidity_rank_percentile", 

    "ANS_crude_pct_rank_percentile", 
    "MgSO_crude_pct_rank_percentile", 
    "DCC_crude_pct_rank_percentile",
    "normothermia_crude_pct_rank_percentile",
    
    "bpd_crude_pct_rank_percentile",
    "NEC_crude_pct_rank_percentile",
    "sepsis_crude_pct_no_zeros_rank_percentile",
    "IVH_crude_pct_rank_percentile",
    "cPVL_crude_pct_rank_percentile"
    )

desired_deciles <- 10
break_points <- seq(0, 100, length.out = desired_deciles + 1)

for(pred in predictors_to_decile){
  binned_name <- paste0(pred, "_decile")
  
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse[[binned_name]] <- cut(
    NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse[[pred]],
    breaks = break_points,
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    labels = 1:desired_deciles
  )
  
  # Optional: make numeric (brms can handle integers)
  NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse[[binned_name]] <- as.integer(as.character(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse[[binned_name]]))
  
  cat(pred, ": created", length(unique(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse[[binned_name]])), "bins\n")
}


head(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse[, c(predictors_to_decile, paste0(predictors_to_decile, "_decile"))])
```

```{r, bayesian model to predict death from perinatal composite factors with 10 bins}
library(brms)

brms_decile_model <- brm(
  StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_rank_percentile_decile ~
      mean_perinatal_rank_percentile_decile +   
    Unit_level_highest +
    (1 | Trust_name) ,
  
  data = NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse,
  family = cumulative("logit"),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 15)
)

brms_decile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank <- brms_decile_model
summary(brms_decile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank)


```
