```{r, extract a word file from all of our bayesian models }
for (decimal_places in c(1, 2, 3)){
library(brms)
library(flextable)
library(officer)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

global_table <- NULL
max_rows <- 0 #this will get updated within the loop
table_list <- list()

pad_rows <- function(df, target_rows) {
  n_missing <- target_rows - nrow(df)
  if(n_missing > 0){
    # create empty rows with same columns
    empty_rows <- df[rep(NA, n_missing), ]
    rownames(empty_rows) <- NULL
    df <- rbind(df, empty_rows)
  }
  return(df)
}

for (name_of_model_to_extract in c(
  "brms_decile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank",
  "brms_decile_model_NEC_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank",
  "brms_decile_model_bpd_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank",
  "brms_decile_model_sepsis_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank",
  "brms_decile_model_IVH_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank",
  "brms_decile_model_cPVL_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank"
  )){
model_to_extract <- get(name_of_model_to_extract)
summary_of_model <- summary(model_to_extract)

if (grepl("NEC", name_of_model_to_extract)) {
  outcome_variable <- "NEC"
} else if (grepl("bpd", name_of_model_to_extract)) {
  outcome_variable <- "bpd"
} else if (grepl("IVH", name_of_model_to_extract)) {
  outcome_variable <- "IVH"
} else if (grepl("cPVL", name_of_model_to_extract)) {
  outcome_variable <- "cPVL"
} else if (grepl("sepsis", name_of_model_to_extract)) {
  outcome_variable <- "sepsis"
} else {
  outcome_variable <- "death"  # fallback if no match
}

coefficients <- 
  rownames_to_column(
    as.data.frame(brms::fixef(model_to_extract)), var="Predictor")

random_sd <- (VarCorr(model_to_extract)$Trust_name$sd)

random_sd_for_table <- 
  paste0(round(random_sd[1], decimal_places), 
    " (", 
       round(random_sd[3], decimal_places),
    " to ", 
       round(random_sd[4], decimal_places),
    ")")

number_observations <- nobs(model_to_extract)

number_trusts <- as.numeric(summary_of_model$ngrps)

#now create a table fixing decimal points and putting credible interval into brackets for raw coefficients

raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  data.frame(
  
  Predictor= as.character(coefficients$Predictor),
  
  Estimate = paste0(
    round(coefficients$Estimate, decimal_places),
    " (", 
    round(coefficients$Q2.5, decimal_places),
    " to ", 
    round(coefficients$Q97.5, decimal_places),
    ")"
  ),
  
  Odds_ratios = paste0(
    round(exp(coefficients$Estimate), decimal_places),
    " (", 
    round(exp(coefficients$Q2.5), decimal_places),
    " to ", 
    round(exp(coefficients$Q97.5), decimal_places),
    ")"
  )
)


#add some rows to our raw coefficients
raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  raw_coefficients_to_print %>% add_row(Predictor = " ", Estimate = " ", Odds_ratios = " ", .before = 1)

raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  raw_coefficients_to_print %>% add_row(Predictor = "Outcome", Estimate = outcome_variable, Odds_ratios = outcome_variable, .before = 1)

raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  raw_coefficients_to_print %>% add_row(Predictor = " ", Estimate = " ", Odds_ratios = " ")

raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  raw_coefficients_to_print %>% add_row(Predictor = "Number of observations", Estimate = as.character(number_observations), Odds_ratios = as.character(number_observations))

raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  raw_coefficients_to_print %>% add_row(Predictor = "Number of trusts", Estimate = as.character(number_trusts), Odds_ratios = as.character(number_trusts))

raw_coefficients_to_print <- 
  raw_coefficients_to_print %>% add_row(Predictor = "SD of random intercepts", Estimate = as.character(random_sd_for_table), Odds_ratios = as.character(random_sd_for_table))

  # update max_rows
  max_rows <- max(max_rows, nrow(raw_coefficients_to_print))
  
  # store in a list temporarily
  table_list[[name_of_model_to_extract]] <- raw_coefficients_to_print

# Create a flextable from the frequency table
ft <- flextable(raw_coefficients_to_print)

# Customize the table appearance 
ft <- ft %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  align(align = "center", part = "header") %>%
  autofit()

# Define paragraph formatting with centered alignment
centered_paragraph <- 
  fp_par(text.align = "center")
# Define font properties (e.g., larger font size)
font_properties <- fp_text(font.size = 14, bold = TRUE, color = "black")
# Save the table to a Word document
doc <- 
  read_docx() %>%
  body_add_flextable(ft)

  
  dir.create("word_tables", showWarnings = F)
  
print(doc, 
      target = paste0("word_tables/", name_of_model_to_extract, "_", decimal_places, "dp", ".docx"))

}}
```

```{r, graph and lmer overall mortality on overall rank multilevel illustrative model no interaction on unit parallel lines}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom.mixed)
library(dplyr)
library(performance)

lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank <- 
  lmer(
    StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_rank_percentile ~ 
                    mean_perinatal_rank_percentile +
                    Unit_level_highest_character +
                    (1 | Trust_name)  ,
    data=NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse)
summary(lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank)
dir.create("model_outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
confidence_intervals <- 
  as.data.frame(confint(lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank, method = "profile"))

tidy_fixed <- tidy(lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank, effects = "fixed") %>%
  select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value)

# Save to CSV
write.csv(tidy_fixed, "model_outputs/lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank_fixed.csv", row.names = FALSE)

data_used <- subset(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse, 
                    !is.na(StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_rank_percentile) &
                    !is.na(mean_perinatal_rank_percentile) &
                    !is.na(Unit_level_highest_character))

data_used$prediction <- 
  predict(lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank, re.form = NA)

table <- table(data_used$Year)
table_unit_level <- table(data_used$Unit_level_highest_character)

length(data_used$Year)

# Save console summary to a text file 
sink("model_outputs/lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank.txt", split = TRUE)
print(summary(lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank))
performance::r2(lmer_percentile_model_death_on_perinatal_predictors_trust_rank)
print("Confidence intervals of random effects:")

print(as.numeric(confidence_intervals[".sig01",][1]))
print(as.numeric(confidence_intervals[".sig01",][2]))

print("Data within each year:")

paste(paste(names(table), table, sep=":"), collapse = ", ")

print("Data from each unit:")

paste(paste(names(table_unit_level), table_unit_level, sep=":"), collapse = ", ")
sink()

regression_plot <-
ggplot(
  data=data_used, 
  aes(x=mean_perinatal_rank_percentile, y=StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_rank_percentile, colour=Unit_level_highest_character)) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
  "1" = "Orange",
  "2018" = "SkyBlue",
  "2019" = "#009E73", ##009E73 is blueish green
  "2020" = "#F0E442", #yellow #F0E442
  "2" = "#0072B2", #blue #0072B2
  "2022" = "#D55E00", ##D55E00 vermillion
  "2023" = "#CC79A7", #purple
  "2024" = "#000000", #black
  "3" = "#000000" #blue #0072B2
  )) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y=prediction), linewidth=1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
  limits = c(0, 100),
  breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20)
) +
  scale_x_continuous(
  limits = c(0, 100),
  breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20)
) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0, 100),
    ylim = c(0, 100)
    ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(  
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())
regression_plot
dir.create("regression_plots")
ggsave(filename = paste0(
  "regression_plot_mortality",
  ".png"),
         path = "regression_plots",
         plot = regression_plot + 
    theme(axis.title=element_blank(), 
         plot.title=element_blank(), 
         plot.subtitle=element_blank(),
         plot.legend=element_blank(),
         legend.position="none"),,
         device = "png",
         width = 3,
         height = 3,
         limitsize = FALSE,
  bg = "white")
getwd()
```

```{r, box plot for figure 1}
         path = "box_plots",
         plot = box_plot + 
    theme(axis.title=element_blank(), 
         plot.title=element_blank(), 
         plot.subtitle=element_blank()),,

         height = 3,
```

***************
loop in colour histograms
***************

```{r, dynamic histogram  colour saves all separate plots in folder histograms}
NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse$Year <- 
  as.character(NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse$Year)

for (type in c(
  "crude"
)){
  
for (x_variable in c(
  "normothermia_crude_pct",
  "StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate",
  "ANS_crude_pct",
  "MgSO_crude_pct",
  "bpd_crude_pct",
  "DCC_crude_pct",
  "NEC_crude_pct",
  "sepsis_crude_pct_no_zeros",
  "IVH_crude_pct",
  "cPVL_crude_pct"
)){

flexible_bin_width <- 0.5

if (type=="rank"){
  flexible_bin_width <- 0.01
  x_variable <- paste0(x_variable, "_rank_norm")
}
#tweak the bin width to be smaller for individual predictors or outcomes:
if (x_variable=="sepsis_crude_pct_no_zeros" | 
    x_variable=="IVH_crude_pct" | 
    x_variable=="StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate"){
  flexible_bin_width <- 0.1
}
  
histogram_loop <-
  ggplot(
      data = NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse, 
      aes(x = !!sym(x_variable), fill=Year)) +
    geom_histogram(
      binwidth = flexible_bin_width, 
      linewidth = linewidth_for_histograms,
      color = "white",
      alpha = 1,
      fill="white") +
  geom_histogram(
      binwidth = flexible_bin_width, 
      linewidth = linewidth_for_histograms,
      color = "white",
      alpha = alpha_for_histograms) +
  labs(title=x_variable) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
  "2017" = "Orange",
  "2018" = "SkyBlue",
  "2019" = "#009E73", ##009E73 is blueish green
  "2020" = "#F0E442", #yellow #F0E442
  "2021" = "#0072B2", #blue #0072B2
  "2022" = "#D55E00", ##D55E00 vermillion
  "2023" = "#CC79A7", #purple
  "2024" = "#000000" #black
  )) +
  theme_minimal() 
histogram_loop

ggsave(filename = paste0(
  x_variable,
  ".png"),
         path = "histograms",
         plot = histogram_loop,
         device = "png",
         width = 6,
         height = 3,
         limitsize = FALSE,
  bg = "white")



ggsave(filename = paste0(
  x_variable,
  "_blank.png"),
         path = "histograms",
         plot = histogram_loop +
    theme(axis.title=element_blank(), 
         plot.title=element_blank(), 
         plot.subtitle=element_blank()),
         device = "png",
         width = 6,
         height = 3,
         limitsize = FALSE,
  bg = "white")

}}
```

********************************************************************************************************************************************
Multilevel illustrative model for paper and summary statistics for paper
*********************************************************************************************************************************************

```{r, give me summary statistics}
years <- 2017:2024
cols  <- 
  c(
    "StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate", 
    "ANS_crude_pct", 
    "MgSO_crude_pct", 
    "normothermia_crude_pct", 
    "DCC_crude_pct", 
    "bpd_crude_pct", 
    "NEC_crude_pct", 
    "sepsis_crude_pct", 
    "IVH_crude_pct", 
    "cPVL_crude_pct"
    ) 

summary_statistics <- data.frame(variable = cols, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

for (yr in years) {

  df <- get(paste0("NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_check_", yr))

  # compute summaries for each variable
  summaries <- sapply(cols, function(col) {
    x <- df[[col]]
    sprintf("%.1f\n(%.1f to %.1f)\nn = %d",
            median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(!is.na(x)))
  })

  # add as a new column named by year
  summary_statistics[[as.character(yr)]] <- summaries
}

summary_statistics
dir.create("summary_statistics")
write.csv(summary_statistics, "summary_statistics/summary_statistics_table_1.csv", row.names = F)
```

```{r, lower part of table 1 with unit level summary statistics}
years <- 2017:2024
levels_ordered <- c("1", "2", "3")   # forced order

unit_level_statistics <- data.frame(
  Unit_level_highest_character = levels_ordered,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (yr in years) {

  df <- get(paste0("NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_check_", yr))

  # restrict to rows with stabilised rate available
  df_filtered <- df[!is.na(df$StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate), ]

  # tabulate unit levels
  tab <- table(df_filtered$Unit_level_highest_character)

  # force ordering; missing levels become 0
  year_counts <- sapply(levels_ordered, function(lvl) {
    if (lvl %in% names(tab)) tab[[lvl]] else 0
  })

  unit_level_statistics[[as.character(yr)]] <- year_counts
}

unit_level_statistics

write.csv(unit_level_statistics, "summary_statistics/unit_level_statistics_table_1.csv")
```


********************************
ranking tables for supplementary
********************************

```{r, create ranking tables of trusts for each year}
print("Note that in this frame, we rank by our rank norm, not our percentiles. Because top rank is best, instead of top percentile being best")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(flextable)
library(officer)
dir.create("ranking_tables")
for (metric_to_rank_by in c(
  "StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_no_ties",
  "mean_perinatal_rank_norm_no_ties"
)) {
  
  
  # Map metric name to human-readable title
  title <- switch(
    metric_to_rank_by,
      "StabilisedNeonatalDeathRate_no_ties" = "Stabilised neonatal death rate",
      "mean_perinatal_rank_norm_no_ties" = "Normalised rank of mean of perinatal NNAP metrics"
  )
  
# Create a dynamic column name by pasting "Rank: " with title
  rank_col_name <- paste0("Rank: ", title)
  
  abbreviations_to_join <- read.csv("abbreviations_to_load/Abbreviations_to_load.csv")
  
NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse_with_abbreviations <-
  dplyr::left_join(
    NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse,
    abbreviations_to_join,
    by = c("Trust_name" = "Trust")
  )

rank_table <- NNAP_and_MBRRACE_data_to_analyse_with_abbreviations %>%
    filter(Year %in% 2017:2024) %>%
    select(
      Year,
      !!rank_col_name := !!sym(metric_to_rank_by),  # dynamic column name
      Abbreviation
    ) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    group_by(!!sym(rank_col_name), Year) %>%
    summarise(Abbreviation = paste(Abbreviation, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Year,
      values_from = Abbreviation
    ) %>%
    arrange(!!sym(rank_col_name))

# Replace NAs with "No data" in the dynamic rank column
rank_table <- rank_table %>%
  mutate(
    !!rank_col_name := as.character(!!sym(rank_col_name)),  # convert to character
    !!rank_col_name := replace_na(!!sym(rank_col_name), "No data")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    rank_table, 
    file = paste0("ranking_tables/rank_by_", metric_to_rank_by, ".csv"), 
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  #we want to write our ranking table to a word file
# Create a flextable from the frequency table
ft <- flextable(rank_table)

# Customize the table appearance (optional)
ft <- ft %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  align(align = "center", part = "header") %>%
  autofit()

# Define paragraph formatting with centered alignment
centered_paragraph <- 
  fp_par(text.align = "center")
# Define font properties (e.g., larger font size)
font_properties <- fp_text(font.size = 14, bold = TRUE, color = "black")
# Save the table to a Word document
doc <- 
  read_docx() %>%
  body_add_flextable(ft) 

  
  dir.create("ranking_tables", showWarnings = F)
  
print(doc, 
      target = paste0("ranking_tables/", "rankings_by_", metric_to_rank_by, ".docx"))


}
```
